column1: # Pattern rules, applied only where `physical-object-classification.tsv` has no
# explicit line for the object. Rules are data on purpose: classifying a family
# of objects is then a reviewed diff, not a source edit.
#   schema        : exact schema name, or * for any
#   name_pattern  : PowerShell -like pattern (use * as wildcard), matched case-sensitively
#   logical_family: the product family this object belongs to
#   owner         : the worker or role accountable for it
# ORDER MATTERS: the first matching rule wins, so put specific patterns above
# general ones. A rule that matches nothing is reported by the generator, because
# a dead rule is a rule somebody believes is protecting something.
# This file does not attempt to classify every object in the database. It covers
# the families whose membership is derivable from a naming convention that the
# product already enforces. Everything else is left UNCLASSIFIED on purpose, so
# that the first census reports the true size of the adjudication rather than
# hiding it behind a catch-all rule. A trailing `*  *  *` rule would make this
# gate green and meaningless; do not add one.
